comments.quote_zh: 这 1250 美元让我赚到钱
comments.text_zh: 请看看这个：《Fuck You, Pay Me》：[VIDEO] 我曾经花 1250 美元请一位商业律师为我的服务协议起草了一份模板，这是我过去 7 年里花得最值的 1250 美元。这 1250 美元让我赚到钱，因为我从来不必追着客户催款，因为他们知道如果不付款，我有法律途径可走。自那以后，我大概又付给他 1000 美元，处理客户想在我的服务协议中修订（redline）的地方。总共 2250 美元（这是合法的业务支出），与一张未付发票会让我损失的金额相比，简直微不足道。与此同时，我总是听到自由职业者说拿不到钱，却又声称律师“太贵了”。你知道真正贵的是什么吗？是你过去 N 天的工作只拿到 0 美元，而不是 X 美元。X 美元可要多得多，而且除非你有合同在手，否则每次和客户合作，你都把自己暴露在这种可能性之下。
comments.text: Please watch this: Fuck You, Pay Me: [VIDEO] The $1250 I spent once to have a business attorney draft up a template for my services agreement is the best $1250 I ever spent in the past 7 years. That $1250 makes me money , because I never have to harass clients to get paid, because they know I have legal recourse if they don't. Since then I've maybe paid him $1000 to deal with things clients wanted to redline in my service agreement. That $2250 total (which is a legitimate business expense) is a pittance compared to what I would lose for a single unpaid invoice. Meanwhile, I always hear from freelancers that don't get paid, but claim lawyers are "too expensive". You know what's really expensive? Getting $0 for the last N days you worked instead of $X. $X is a hell of a lot more money, and unless you have a contract in place, you expose yourself to that possibility every time you engage with a client.

comments.story_title: Fucking Sue Me (2011)
comments.why_zh: 如何借助律师谈判过时的模板合同条款。
comments.quote_zh: 他说很多公司都有模板合同，其中包含过时的条款
comments.text_zh: 这真的要看情况；有些公司的法务部门可能会对他们要求你签署的东西做得太过火，“不签就不合作”。Mike Monteiro 在他的“Fuck you, pay me”演讲中谈到了这一点 [1]。他说很多公司都有模板合同，其中包含过时的条款，比如要求你交出源代码打印件，或者用软盘交付软件。正确的应对是自己请一位律师，由他审阅合同，并向公司的法务顾问解释：1）这些合同条款不合理且过时；2）删掉这些条款不会给公司带来额外责任。这些合同之所以会做得过火，是因为公司每次吃亏，就会在合同里加一道“疤痕”，防止同样的事件再次发生，而不管它是否适用于手头的任务。也许世界各地情况不同，但我们过去签过一些疯狂的东西（不签就是交易告吹），而且从来没人因此起诉我们。我说句大实话。你只是运气好。你把头伸进了狮子嘴里，而它没有咬下去。这并不意味着你做的事是个好主意，只意味着你侥幸逃脱了。[1]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: That really depends; some company's legal department might go overboard with the stuff they make you sign 'or no deal'. Mike Monteiro talks about this in his "Fuck you, pay me" talk [1]. He says that a lot of companies have boilerplate contracts which have outdated provisions like requiring you to hand over printouts of source code, or delivering software on floppy diskettes. The proper response is to have a lawyer yourself who can review the contract and explain to the company's legal counsel that 1) these contract provisions are unreasonable and outdated and 2) that striking these provisions will not create additional liabilities for the company. The reasons these contracts go overboard is because every time the company gets burned, it adds some scar tissue to the contract to prevent that same eventually from occurring again, regardless of whether it's applicable to the task at hand. Maybe it works different in different parts of the world, but we signed some crazy things (which were dealbreakers if not signed) in the past and no-one ever sued us for it I will be extremely honest. You got lucky. You put your head in the mouth of the lion, and it didn't bite. It doesn't mean that what you did was a good idea, it just means that you got away with it. [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ClearAndPresent
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Freelancer's Dilemma – Client Won't Pay Despite Clear Agreement
comments.why_zh: 应对不付款客户的心态。
comments.text_zh: 作为清口菜和腰梁：[VIDEO]（你已经猜到是 Mike Monteiro 了。）就这个项目而言：他们是主动拒付（“我们不会付你钱。”），还是被动拒付（不回邮件）？后者可能只是无能。就像其他人提到的，具体法律建议取决于各自司法辖区，但一封正式的律师函有时能在财务部门拖沓时把法务叫醒。你交付了代码/服务器/凭据的最终访问权限吗？如果没有，在最终付款前，温和地让服务器、DBs、平台暂停运行。以后的项目：一定要签合同。一定要有启动预付款。在初次报价里把自己价格报高一些，并要求分阶段付款，这样当你的交付进度完成 50-75% 时，你已经 100% 收到款。你掌控源代码账户，你掌控服务器凭据，你掌控数据库访问凭据，等最终支票到账后你再移交最终访问权限。
comments.text: As a palette cleanser and loin girder: [VIDEO] (You already guessed it was Mike Monteiro.) For this project: Did they refuse to pay actively ("We won't pay you."), or passively (No replies to emails.) The latter might be incompetence. As others mentioned, specific legal advice depends on respective jurisdictions, but an offical lawyer's letter sometimes wakes up legal when accounting is drifting. Did you deliver the final access to the code / server / credentials? If not, gently bring servers, DBs, platforms to a halt pending final payments. Future projects: Contract, always. Up-front commencement payments, always. Price yourself higher in the initial quote, and ask for staged payments, such that by the time your delivery schedule is 50-75% done you are 100% paid. You control the source code accounts, you control the server credentials, you control the database access credentials, you hand over final access after the final check has cleared.

comments.text_zh: 哦，你刚刚唤醒了我做自由职业者时的美好回忆。作为自由职业者，有时很难绕过这个简单的观念：你就是你自己的公司，你必须像公司一样行事：不惜一切代价保护和捍卫你的工作。我浪费了几个月时间、价值几千美元的工作被偷走之后，才接受我必须改变自己行为的事实。作为自由职业者，你大致有两种做法：- 尽早设定边界，没有预先定义并商定的首付款就不要开始任何工作；如果工作超过几天，就按需设定里程碑并要求付款。- 找律师，对客户保持灵活（付款延迟对任何公司都是常见情况），但不要害怕追讨不诚实的客户；如果你负担不起或不想走这条路，那你需要提前尽可能设置更多应急措施（见上一点）。一个经典视频可能帮你进入正确心态：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Oh you just revived sweet memories of my times as a freelancer. As a freelancer, it's sometimes hard to get around the simple idea that you are your own company and that you must act like one: protect and defend your work at all cost. It took me months of time wasted, and thousands of dollars of work stolen to accept the fact I need to change my behaviour, as a freelancer you have roughly two approaches: - set boundaries early on, don't start any work with a predefined and agreed upon down payment, if the work is more than a few days long: set milestones as need be with payments required. - lawyer up, be flexible with clients (delays in payments are a common occurrence with any company) but don't be afraid to go after dishonest clients, if you can't afford it or don't feel like going this path then you need to set up as many contingencies as possible upfront (see previous point). A classic video that might help you get in the right mindset: [VIDEO]

comments.author: davismwfl
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Slow paying client and how do you deal with them?
comments.why_zh: 谈论如何让付款缓慢的客户付钱。
comments.text_zh: 这种情况我经历过很多次了。你总会遇到这样的客户，以下是我目前为止找到的最好的办法。1：除非客户已经证明了自己的信用，或者通过了信用审核，否则不要给 net 30 天的账期。对大型公司可以有一些例外，但很多中小企业在付款方面非常糟糕。大企业可能动作慢一点，但几乎总是稳定地付款，除非出现了已知的问题。2：如果你确实给了 net 30 天账期（或者任何超过 10 天的账期），那就为 10 天内付款提供折扣。这几乎能让所有较大的企业优先处理你的发票，把钱付给你。你可能觉得这微不足道，但很多企业在成百上千、有时是成千上万张发票上都这么做，并因此省下了可观的金额。3：在 TOS/合同中把付款细节写清楚。对于我那些较小的咨询客户，如果发票在到期日之后 3 天仍未付款，我就会停止所有工作，他们也会失去服务排队的位次。所以基本上这些客户大多只有 7 到 10 天的时间付款，否则我就停工。我还事先说明，如果这种情况在短期内（在合同中定义）发生 2 次，那么未来所有工作（如果我还接的话）都将改为预付款。这是我不容谈判的合同条款之一。对于我的 SaaS 产品，我用了类似的条款，我们对中小客户（通常每月低于 2k 美元）直接刷他们的信用卡，如果卡被拒，或者我们无法在该月服务开始 5 天后完成收款
comments.text: I have lived this many times over. You will always have clients like this, these are the best ways I have found so far. 1: do not give net 30 day terms unless a client has earned them or applied via credit. Some exceptions can be made for large firms, but many small to medium businesses are terrible about paying. Large businesses might be a little slow, but almost always pay consistently the same, unless there is a known issue. 2: If you do give net 30 terms (or anything more then 10 days), provide a discount for payment within 10 days. This makes almost all larger businesses prioritize your invoice and get you paid. You may think it is minor, but many businesses do this over hundreds or sometimes thousands of invoices and they save significant amounts of money doing so. 3: Make payment details clear within your TOS/contract. For my smaller consulting clients, if their invoice was unpaid after 3 days from the due date I stopped all work and they lost their spot in line for services. So essentially most of those clients had 7-10 days to pay me or I halted all work. I also had it up front that if that happened 2 times within a short period (defined in the contract) that all future work (if accepted) would be prepaid. This was part of my non-negotiable contract terms. comments.text_zh: >要么付钱，要么别干活。作为一名目前自己停了工的电工（因为对方既不付钱又玩失踪，两个月没联系了，到现在还是这样），我一步不让。你连着两次没来我们约定的现场碰头（而且到现在也没联系我），我本来想申请留置权……但后来决定干脆让你租不出去（不给你把空调/水/电弄完）。你总会抽空处理的吧……？当我跟这个 LLC/业主说「你显然不急，因为你显然既没来工地也没来找我」时，我还以为他几天内会露面。然后变成几周。现在眼看要几个月了。你手里有我一堆待办清单（一直没解决），我手里有一堆问题（你到底想怎么样？），而你连开个水电这种小事都不肯做。去你妈的，给钱。[•] < [VIDEO] >
comments.text: >Be paid or don't work. As an electrician currently self-stopped (for both non-payment & absenteeism, two months no contact , so far) I'm not budging. When you didn't show up for our last two on-site meetups (and still haven't contacted), I thought about filing a lien... but decided to just keep you from having tenants (by not finishing AC/water/electric). You'll get around to it..? When I told this LLC/owner "you obviously aren't in a rush because you obviously aren't visiting the jobsite/me" I sort of expected him to show within a few days. Then a few weeks. And now we're entering a few months. You have weeks of my punchlists (unresolved to do ), I have weeks of questions (what do you want ?) and you won't even do simple things like turning on power/water. Fuck you, pay me. [•] < [VIDEO] >
